title: Zephyrine and the Harvest
premise: Folklorist Zephyrine Amberdale has spent three years in the village of Hollowmere documenting songs no one will sing twice, rationalizing the noises beneath the fields as wind, water, settling earth. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, the village's careful forgetting begins to unravel, and Zephyrine learns the harvest is not of crops but of residents, counted and claimed by something that has owned the land for centuries. Falling in love with Merrin, the last resident who has not yet signed her family's papers, Zephyrine must choose between his duty to record and preserve—and his duty to get her family out before the count completes. In the end, he burns his field recordings as an offering, breaks the count by refusing to name what he loves, and escapes with Merrin as Hollowmere seals itself behind them, taking its songs forever.
about_author: Yara Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in rural communities before turning to fiction. They write horror about the things villages agree not to remember.

chapters.title: The Songs That Refuse
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He records an elderly singer who stops mid-verse, pale, insisting she never learned the rest. The emotional beat: quiet unease disguised as academic curiosity; Zephyrine files the interruption away as stage fright.

chapters.title: Three Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A catalogue of rationalizations: the knocking under the churchyard is water pipes, the humming at dusk is bees. He drafts a letter home he never sends. Emotional beat: loneliness dressed up as dedication.

chapters.title: Merrin Amberdale
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He meets Merrin, who shares his surname by coincidence neither can explain, tending a garden that grows out of season. Their conversation sparks warmth and recognition. Emotional beat: first belonging.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Crews break ground on the old common field; the foreman complains the soil 'gives back' their shovels at night. Zephyrine watches from the ridge, notebook empty for the first time. Emotional beat: dread arriving without evidence.

chapters.title: A Door Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The crew unearths a stone door whose hinges are rusted shut—on the inside. Scratches line the inner face. The village goes silent around him. Emotional beat: the collapse of every explanation he has built.

chapters.title: What the Village Won't Say
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He presses the publican about local history and receives identical, rehearsed answers from three different people. That night someone leaves a dead crow on his doorstep. Emotional beat: realizing invisibility was protection, and it's over.

chapters.title: Merrin's Papers
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. She reveals her family holds documents—deeds signed generations ago, renewed each harvest by 'the last resident.' Her grandmother died before signing this year's. Emotional beat: fear braided with tenderness toward Zephyrine.

chapters.title: The Count Begins
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At dusk, voices in the field call names; each named villager answers involuntarily, standing at their window. The count reaches nineteen and pauses. Emotional beat: horror becoming arithmetic.

chapters.title: Songs Sung Twice
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Desperate, he plays back his recordings; the songs continue past where the singers stopped, in voices not theirs. He understands the recordings are listening back. Emotional beat: his life's work revealed as a trap.

chapters.title: The Family Tree
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. She shows Zephyrine the family ledger: every generation includes an outsider who married in, recorded, or simply stayed too long. His own arrival date is written there—in ink older than his visit. Emotional beat: love shadowed by fatalism.

chapters.title: Nineteen and One
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The count resumes: twenty names, and the twentieth is his. Merrin lies to the dark on his behalf, and the voice accepts it—for now. Emotional beat: terror and gratitude entangled; duty to self versus duty to her.

chapters.title: Leaving Is a Kind of Signing
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. They plan escape, but the roads loop back to Hollowmere; the bus driver apologizes, eyes forward, and returns them. Emotional beat: claustrophobic despair—the village will not permit departure unsigned.

chapters.title: The Under-Singer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Through the unearthed door he hears the source: something singing the villagers' songs in reverse, patient, learning them. It knows his name now. Emotional beat: confrontation with the scale of what owns Hollowmere.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Last Verse
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Among her grandmother's effects, Merrin finds an unfinished verse meant to end the count—a song of refusal. Half the lines are missing. Emotional beat: fragile hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: The Village Chooses
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The villagers, desperate to be spared, offer Zephyrine to the field themselves. Neighbors he interviewed for three years hold lanterns at the lane's end. Emotional beat: betrayal; belonging revealed as ownership.

chapters.title: What Love Refuses to Name
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Merrin realizes the count works through naming—that claiming requires a name spoken willingly. If she refuses to name what she loves, it cannot be counted. Emotional beat: clarity purchased at the edge of grief.

chapters.title: The Papers Burn
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine burns the family deeds and his own recordings together; the fire sings. The count falters at nineteen, then begins again, angrier. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy—destroying the archive to free the living.

chapters.title: The Last Resident Signs
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Cornered, Merrin signs the papers—but writes no name, only the unfinished verse of refusal. The ink runs backward. The ground opens along the old common. Emotional beat: defiance as climax; the harvest denied.

chapters.title: Hollowmere Closes Its Door
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The village turns inward, houses folding toward the field like a hand closing. The under-singer takes the whole settlement rather than lose the count. Zephyrine and Merrin run the ridge road as dawn breaks. Emotional beat: escape through ruin.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Weeks later, in a coastal town, they find no trace of Hollowmere on any map. Zephyrine cannot remember the songs—which is the point. Emotional beat: hollow relief, survival with amputated memory.

chapters.title: The Verse Merrin Keeps
chapters.summary: Merrin's POV. Merrin discovers she retained one line of her grandmother's verse, and hums it to their garden, which grows out of season. Something far below hums back—not hungry, only listening. Emotional beat: uneasy peace; belonging rebuilt on new terms.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Years on, they return to the valley's edge each autumn and leave an unnamed offering. The field stays fallow, the door stays shut, and the count stands forever at nineteen. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved—some debts are kept paid, never settled.
